findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 30% to 70% lightness
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch uses 70%, which noticeably lightens the embedded-post username links in light themes. The dark branch uses 30% instead of the complementary 70%. The two values appear swapped; the expected form is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

findings.title: Light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% lightness
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new light branch uses 30%, which makes the custom-message-length text much darker in light themes. The dark-branch value is also inverted. The expected form is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)).

findings.title: topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), but it was replaced with 50%/50%. This changes the light-theme appearance, which a refactor limited to dark themes should not do. The expected form is dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)).

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was 30%; the new light branch uses 50%. This alters the light-theme color, which should stay the same. It should be 30% for light and 70% for the $secondary branch.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same regression as the desktop file: the original light-theme value of 30% was replaced with 50%. It should be dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).
